title: Module tour
subtitle: Zigzag walks the stack.
disclaimer: Stylized planetarium tour — not an official NASA briefing.

beats.text: Welcome aboard. I am Zigzag. This kite of metal is your International Space Station. We will walk it room by room.
Destiny. The American laboratory. Racks of biology and materials science, and the brains of the U.S. segment.
Harmony, Node 2. Crew Dragon docks on the ram port. Four sleep stations. This is where most visiting crews hang their sleeping bags.
Starboard, Columbus. Europe’s lab. Short, dense, and full of fluid physics. ESA built it; NASA flew it up on a shuttle.
Port side, the JEM Pressurized Module. ELM-PS is the storage attic on the zenith. The JEM airlock passes payloads out to JEM-EF, the Exposed Facility, where JEMRMS sets them on the porch.
Nadir now. Cupola. Seven windows, Earth filling the glass. This is where they fly the Canadian arm and watch weather crawl.
Aft, Zvezda. The Russian home. Engines, a table, sleep nooks. The station still reboosts from here.
Pull the rooms apart and you see the joints. Unity in the middle. Truss on top. Solar wings like a dragonfly. That is the whole animal.
